title: Letter 16 — Fear Only God
attribution_note: Letter 16 of 46 in the collection Letters Sent — see Letter 1 for provenance.

pairs.en: *“My friend and brother in Christ!”*

Often I hear David the saint sing: *“There were they in great fear, where no fear was”* [Psalm 13:5]. And not understanding what this song meant, I pondered it many a time. But then my spirit felt that it means this: that men fear man, but do not fear God; they fear *“them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul,”* but do not fear Him *“which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell”* [Matthew 10:28]; they fear to lose temporal life, but do not fear to lose eternal life; they fear to be deprived of wealth, glory, honour and pleasure, but do not fear to be deprived of eternal blessings, honour, glory and the consolation of paradise; they fear bonds, prison and temporal exile, but do not fear eternal prison, bonds and exile; they fear temporal dishonour, but do not fear eternal dishonour. And so this song befits them: *“There were they in great fear, where no fear was.”*

sections.heading: The fool who says there is no God

pairs.en: And at the beginning of the said psalm he sang: *“The fool hath said in his heart, There is no God”* [Psalm 13:1]. It is the mark, then, of the one who says in his heart, “There is no God,” to fear man, but not to fear God. *“There were they in great fear, where no fear was.”* For one who does not fear the one God must fear everything. *“The wicked flee when no man pursueth”* [Proverbs 28:1]; his conscience is more terrible to him than any persecutor.

But why fear what is not fearful in itself? Every man is such as I am; subject to death and to every woe, as I am; weak as I am, and all that is in him is as it is in me. Satan, the spirit of malice and my enemy, is unseen by me, yet known to me by the presence of his evil counsels; he is terrible — but without the will of God he has no power, not only over me, a man, but even over beasts and swine (cf. Matthew 8:31); and the same is true of every man who wars against me.

Why, again, fear to lose what one must of necessity lose? Wealth, honour, glory and every treasure of this world will pass from us, whether we fear to lose them or not: death strips all this from us. Fear death, or do not fear it — you will not escape death. No one will cast me into exile, into prison, into bonds without God; and if they do, know that God has signed it so. No one will strip me of wealth, honour or glory without God; and if they do, know that it has so pleased God.

*“As it shall please the Lord, so let it be”* [Job 1:21]. God holds all things in His hand, and nothing comes to pass without Him, whatever befalls us. And nothing proceeds from Him but good — as light from the sun, warmth from fire, and mercy and kindness from love. He bestows His good upon us because He is good. He suffers the devil, and evil men, and through them calamity, affliction and temptation, to come upon us — but according to the measure of our strength, as much as we are able to bear; and all of it He permits for our good, because He is good. For from the true and eternal Good, nothing proceeds but true good.

Why, then, should I fear what is unavoidable for me? If God permits a calamity to befall me, I shall not escape it: it will come upon me, though I fear it. But if He does not allow it, then though all the devils, and all evil men, and the whole world rise up, they can do nothing to me — for He alone, who is mightier than all, *“shall turn evil upon mine enemies”* [Psalm 53:7]. Fire will not burn, the sword will not cut, water will not drown, the earth will not swallow up, without God: for all, as creation, without the command of its Creator, can do nothing.

Why, then, should I fear all that is, save God? And what God ordains, I shall not escape. Why fear, then, what is unavoidable? Let us fear, then, beloved, the one God alone, that we may fear nothing and no one. For whoever truly fears God fears no one and nothing (read Psalms 25, 32, 33, 35 and 36). Whoever fears the one God finds all things in God; to him God is honour, glory, wealth, consolation, life and all blessedness, though men strip him of honour, glory, wealth, consolation and life. For whoever fears God stands in the favour of God, since he fears to anger and to offend Him.

And whoever stands in God's favour — why should he fear the disfavour and fury of enemies? God is all; and besides God all is nothing, and the malice of all — of devils and of evil men — is nothing. Let them gnash their teeth at him: they can do nothing. *“Blessed is the man that feareth the Lord”* [Psalm 111:1]. Wretched and poor is the man who does not fear the Lord God, for such a one fears everything; *“there were they in great fear, where no fear was.”*

This is what the holy David sang to me, and gladdened my spirit with his sweetest music; and this I send to you from the wilderness. Receive it, dear friend, and strengthen your heart in hope upon God.
